**Contact:** iaeste.lebanon@aub.edu.lb

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > MSFEA CO-OP (Cooperative Education) Handbook > Information for students > The FEAA 500 course]
Topic: MSFEA CO-OP (Cooperative Education) Handbook > Information for students > The FEAA 500 course
### The FEAA 500 course

A student who accepts an offer enrolls in **FEAA 500 in both semesters** of the
co-op position (Summer and Fall, or Spring and Summer):

- **First semester:** register **FEAA 500** (3 credits) and pay its tuition.
- **Second semester:** register **FEAA 500A** (3 credits) with **no additional tuition** (no additional tuition fees).

Full-time student status is maintained in both semesters. A student with
satisfactory performance at the end of the first co-op semester receives a grade
of **"In Progress (PR)"** on FEAA 500; the final **Pass or Fail** grade is
assigned on **FEAA 500A** at the end of the second semester.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > Policies]
## Policies
- **Courses while on co-op:** enrolling in other courses during a co-op is **not
  allowed**, with a possible exception for a Final Year Project (FYP) or
  research-based course (499) if the department allows it and the co-op academic
  advisor (and FYP group members, for an FYP) approve — and only if it does not
  interfere with working hours.
- **Number of credits:** the co-op is a **3-credit Pass/Fail FEAA 500** course.
  Whether it counts toward academic credit, and whether it is treated as a free
  elective or a technical elective, is decided by each department. Students keep
  **full-time student status** during the co-op.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > Policies]
## Policies
- **Tuition / co-op fees:** regular tuition is charged for the 3 credits of FEAA
  500.
- **Approved Experience substitution:** students who pass FEAA 500 are **no longer
  required** to take the Approved Experience / Professional Training course in
  their department (that course is currently billed as 1 credit). Its current course-credit and billing information is maintained
  in the approved internship course clarification, separately from CO-OP tuition.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > Policies]
## Policies
- **Number, duration, and certification:** one placement of at least 6 months is
  required; additional co-ops (consecutive or not) are allowed if approved by the
  department and co-op advisor. A 6-month co-op should typically coincide with the
  **Summer + Fall** or **Spring + Summer** semesters. The co-op appears as a
  course on the academic transcript.
- **Timing and return to campus:** the co-op should take place in the **3rd or 4th
  year** for engineering and graphic design students, and the **4th or 5th year**
  for architecture students. Students must **return to campus for at least one
  term** after their final co-op before graduating.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > Policies]
## Policies
- **Preparation and support:** info sessions, co-op advising weeks, on-demand
  meetings with the co-op CDC Advisor (resume review, counseling, mock
  interviews), the career development modules, access to co-op employers and
  opportunities, follow-up and feedback, and faculty mentorship and assessment.
- **Program length and graduation date:** students may take overloads to complete
  the co-op without delaying graduation, with careful planning and department
  approval. In some cases participation may delay graduation by one term (for one
  co-op).

[summer-training-guidelines-2026.md > Internship Requirements: Duration, Hours, and Locations]
## Internship Requirements: Duration, Hours, and Locations

To qualify for the Bachelor of Engineering degree, you must complete:

- A minimum of 8 full weeks of approved training.
- Typically equivalent to 320 work hours (8 weeks × 40 hours/week).
- Training at a recognized company, organization, laboratory, or approved research setting in Lebanon or abroad.

[summer-training-guidelines-2026.md > Summer Training (Approved Experience) Guidelines > Department-Specific Rules > Industrial Engineering and Management (IEM)]
Topic: Summer Training (Approved Experience) Guidelines > Department-Specific Rules > Industrial Engineering and Management (IEM)
### Industrial Engineering and Management (IEM)

- The standard minimum is 8 full weeks of approved training. Six company weeks alone are insufficient. The research completion route is six company weeks plus 2 weeks of research with an MSFEA faculty member. The alternative two-company route is six company weeks plus a minimum 4-week internship at another company. Both routes require prior approval and documentation. A four-plus-four company plan is not automatically accepted; confirm a different split with the department before relying on it.

[summer-training-guidelines-2026.md > Summer Training (Approved Experience) Guidelines > Internship Requirements: Duration, Hours, and Locations > Internships That Are Not Accepted]
Topic: Summer Training (Approved Experience) Guidelines > Internship Requirements: Duration, Hours, and Locations > Internships That Are Not Accepted
### Internships That Are Not Accepted

Any exception to the internship requirements must be approved through a formal petition. Petitions must:

- Be approved by both the Department and the Course Instructor.
- Include all required supporting documents (incomplete petitions will automatically be rejected).
- Be copied (CC) to the MSFEA Career Development Center (CDC) at fcareer@aub.edu.lb.

Submit petitions through the AUB online petition system: https://petitions.aub.edu.lb


[summer-training-guidelines-2026.md > Summer Training (Approved Experience) Guidelines > Internship Requirements: Duration, Hours, and Locations > Internships That Are Not Accepted]
Topic: Summer Training (Approved Experience) Guidelines > Internship Requirements: Duration, Hours, and Locations > Internships That Are Not Accepted
### Internships That Are Not Accepted

Submit petitions through the AUB online petition system: https://petitions.aub.edu.lb

Your internship should provide meaningful professional experience related to your field of study and allow you to apply engineering or design knowledge in practice. Requirements may vary slightly by department.

history.content: how can an alumini mentro help with careers?

Through MentorPlus+, an alumni mentor connects with you to share insights about their career paths and provide guidance on what to expect professionally. You can learn more about the program at https://www.aub.edu.lb/msfea/Pages/MentorPlus.aspx.
Can you give me the link?

You can find more information about MentorPlus+ at https://www.aub.edu.lb/msfea/Pages/MentorPlus.aspx. 

The sign-up form does not have a direct published link, but you can find the current form on the MSFEA CDC students page at https://www.aub.edu.lb/msfea/cdc/Pages/students.aspx or contact the CDC office at fcareer@aub.edu.lb.
Switching topics: what are my options for an intership overseas?

For an overseas internship, you have the following documented options:

- Standard Approved Experience internship abroad: Complete training at a recognized company, organization, or laboratory overseas for a minimum of 8 full weeks (typically 320 hours at 40 hours per week). Alternatively, you may complete a split option consisting of 6 company weeks plus either 2 weeks of research with an MSFEA faculty member or a second company internship of at least 4 weeks, provided you have prior department approval and documentation.
- IAESTE exchange program: Join the IAESTE Club to participate in international internship exchange opportunities abroad. You can contact them at iaeste.lebanon@aub.edu.lb.
- Remote internship with a U.S.-based company: Allowed if you are legally eligible to work in the U.S. and obtain department approval.

history.content: how can an alumini mentro help with careers?

Through MentorPlus+, an alumni mentor connects with you to share insights about their career paths and provide guidance on what to expect professionally. You can learn more about the program at https://www.aub.edu.lb/msfea/Pages/MentorPlus.aspx.
Can you give me the link?

You can find more information about MentorPlus+ at https://www.aub.edu.lb/msfea/Pages/MentorPlus.aspx. 

The sign-up form does not have a direct published link, but you can find the current form on the MSFEA CDC students page at https://www.aub.edu.lb/msfea/cdc/Pages/students.aspx or contact the CDC office at fcareer@aub.edu.lb.
Switching topics: what are my options for an intership overseas?

For an overseas internship, you have the following documented options:

- Standard Approved Experience internship abroad: Complete training at a recognized company, organization, or laboratory overseas for a minimum of 8 full weeks (typically 320 hours at 40 hours per week). Alternatively, you may complete a split option consisting of 6 company weeks plus either 2 weeks of research with an MSFEA faculty member or a second company internship of at least 4 weeks, provided you have prior department approval and documentation.
- IAESTE exchange program: Join the IAESTE Club to participate in international internship exchange opportunities abroad. You can contact them at iaeste.lebanon@aub.edu.lb.
- Remote internship with a U.S.-based company: Allowed if you are legally eligible to work in the U.S. and obtain department approval.

**Department:** Industrial Engineering and Management (IEM)

**Question/topic:** Is a six-week company internship enough for IEM, or can I combine two company placements?

For an overseas internship, you have the following documented options:

- Standard Approved Experience internship abroad: Complete training at a recognized company, organization, or laboratory overseas for a minimum of 8 full weeks (typically 320 hours at 40 hours per week). ### Applying to an internship found independently
If a student secures an internship on their own (not through the CDC), they must contact the CDC to confirm the company is approved. The CDC will then guide the student to either get the internship confirmed through the CDC, or petition their department directly.

Topic: MSFEA CDC Student Knowledge Base > Career Readiness Resources > Career support overview
### Career support overview

The CDC offers career preparation and support besides internships. Its CV and cover letter guidelines explain how to tailor your resume, use action verbs and present relevant experience professionally. Online modules cover Resume and Cover Letter Writing, Interview Preparation, Work Placement / Job Search, and Workplace Environment and Skills. Career+ is a career-development and certification initiative that helps students explore options and navigate career uncertainty; its paths recognize academic work, applied experience, extracurricular activities and career readiness. MentorPlus+ connects students with AUB alumni for guidance about career paths and professional expectations. For full-time vacancies, students can use the AUB Career Portal and check postings shared by email. The individual sections provide the available links and joining routes; these services have distinct purposes and requirements.

## Approval before beginning an internship

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** Does receiving an internship offer mean I can start and count the placement?

**Answer:** No. Do not assume an offer alone counts as approved training. Offers outside the CDC that lack department pre-approval will not count toward graduation. Complete the Proposal before beginning, and confirm the applicable approval process with the course team before relying on the placement.

[email-clarifications.md > Internship approval authority]
## Internship approval authority

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** Can the chatbot or student assistant approve or authorize my specific internship plan, company, petition, extension, or exception?

**Answer:** No. The student assistant provides policy information only; it cannot grant or verify an individual's formal approval. Internship plans, petitions, and exceptions require decisions by authorized department and course personnel, with the CDC involved as specified by the course process.
